exposure: mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
age at first and last delivery
cohort: The study included 1751 women who delivered in a university hospital over a 5-year period, categorized into those with only cesarean sections and those with at least one vaginal delivery.
finding: The prevalence of urine incontinence was comparable between women who delivered only by cesarean section (5.8%) and those who had at least one vaginal delivery (6.9%), and after adjustment, vaginal delivery was not significantly associated with incontinence compared to cesarean section.
mod_finding: Vaginal and cesarean deliveries were found to have a comparable incidence of urinary incontinence, and after adjustment for other variables, vaginal delivery was not significantly associated with incontinence compared to cesarean.
